catalogue.name: Vizmaya Ledger
catalogue.note: Year, country, typology, scale band, outcome and detection route are seed values from public record, and heat values are seeds that have never been refreshed. Live cases carry the search results they were found in: leads, not verified sources.

families.name: Fraud
families.checks: Where did the story part ways with the cash? Compare reported revenue with operating cash flow, receivable days, collateral counts with lender records, claimed returns with any plausible strategy. Ask who controlled the bank statements, the custodian or the confirmations.
charts: Reported vs verified figure over time (revenue, balances, collateral or assets)
Inflows vs redemptions or new borrowing by period
Months between first red flag and collapse
Recoveries as a share of losses
families.sources: court filings and exhibits, bankruptcy examiner or trustee reports, company filings, auditor reports

families.name: Laundering
families.checks: Source of funds and source of wealth, beneficial ownership, corridors, structuring below thresholds, third-party payments, shell and nominee layers, trade pricing against market, cash intensity. What did the bank know at onboarding and what did monitoring miss?
charts: Flows by corridor and year
Alerts vs suspicious activity reports filed vs prosecutions
Share of volume from the top 10 customers
Penalty as a share of the flows involved
families.sources: enforcement orders, mutual evaluation reports, inquiry reports, leaked-document archives (ICIJ, OCCRP)

families.name: Sanctions and proliferation
families.checks: The legal hook (USD clearing, US persons, controlled items). Ownership and control tests such as the 50 percent rule. Screening gaps. Vessel identity, AIS gaps, ship-to-ship transfers, flag changes. Origin documents against physical flows. Price against any cap.
charts: Shipments or transaction value by quarter
AIS dark periods per voyage
Penalty vs value of the transactions
families.sources: OFAC and BIS enforcement releases, UK OFSI notices, UN panel reports, maritime tracking providers

families.name: Markets
families.checks: Order and trade data, timing against news, price and volume anomalies, communications, positions across related instruments, who benefited, and what surveillance alerts fired and what was done with them.
charts: Price and volume around the key date
Positions vs limits over time
Profit vs penalty
families.sources: SEC, CFTC and exchange surveillance records, trial exhibits, regulator final notices

families.name: Corruption
families.checks: Follow the contract: award process, intermediaries and agents, success fees, shell recipients, politically exposed persons, the gap between award and payment, bank due diligence on those persons, and the hit to the sovereign balance sheet.
charts: Payments to intermediaries vs contract value
Debt raised vs funds received by the project
Amount diverted vs amount recovered
families.sources: DOJ and SEC resolutions, national prosecutor files, parliamentary inquiries, asset recovery reports

families.name: Tax
families.checks: Structure against substance, treaty or withholding arbitrage, the role of advisers and custodians, the date the law changed, who certified what, tax lost against tax recovered.
charts: Tax lost vs recovered by year
Transaction volume vs date of the rule change
families.sources: court judgments, tax authority and parliamentary reports, investigative journalism archives

families.name: Insider and rogue
families.checks: Position limits and breaches, unauthorized trades, fictitious hedges, supervision and mandatory leave, front-office to back-office reconciliation, reported profit against risk taken, access rights and segregation of duties.
charts: Positions vs limits over time
Reported P&L vs risk taken
Losses by month until discovery
families.sources: internal inquiry reports, regulator reports, court records

families.name: Cyber and web3
families.checks: Entry route (key compromise, insider, social engineering, contract bug, oracle or bridge failure, supply chain). Signing and approval design. Hot and cold wallet split. Time from theft to first movement. Laundering path (swaps, bridges, mixers, off-ramps). Freezes and stablecoin blacklists. Funds returned. Who attributed it, on what evidence, and how confident they are. USD value at theft vs today.
charts: Stolen vs frozen vs returned
Time to laundering by hop
Losses by month and attack route
families.sources: incident reports from the victim, FBI and DOJ filings, analytics firms (TRM, Chainalysis, Elliptic, PeckShield, CertiK), block explorers, DefiLlama hacks

families.name: Crime proceeds
families.checks: Placement and layering, cash intensity, front businesses, the human network behind the money, bank exposure, and what the indictment exhibits show about the money route.
charts: Proceeds by route or channel
Seized or forfeited vs estimated proceeds
families.sources: indictments and forfeiture complaints, FATF typology reports, UNODC

families.name: Control failure
families.checks: The four pillars: risk assessment, policies and controls, independent testing, governance and training. Alert volumes and backlogs, tuning decisions, staffing against volume, report timeliness, lookbacks, repeat findings from earlier orders, remediation milestones. Fine as a share of pre-tax profit. Whether any actual crime was found, or only a failure to look.
charts: Alert backlog or reports filed over time
Penalty as a share of pre-tax profit
Repeat findings across successive orders
families.sources: consent orders and final notices, annual reports, monitor reports, regulator speeches

lenses.name: Missed signals
lenses.description: Who saw a warning sign, when, and what happened to them?
lenses.short: Who saw it and said nothing
lenses.focus: Build a missed signals ledger: each warning, who saw it, the date, what they did with it, and what happened to them. Mark each Documented, Contested or Inferred. Count the months between the first warning and the first action.

lenses.name: The loophole
lenses.description: Which rule, gap or blind spot made this possible?
lenses.short: The gap that let it happen
lenses.focus: Name the exact rule, control or supervisory gap. Cite the rule or order by section number if one exists. Say who owned the gap: the firm, a regulator, a statute or the market structure.

lenses.name: Who enabled it
lenses.description: Which banks, auditors, lawyers or regulators made it easier, and what did they gain?
lenses.focus: Map the gatekeepers: banks, auditors, lawyers, trust and company service providers, rating agencies, regulators. For each, say what they saw, what they signed off, what they earned and what happened to them after.

lenses.name: Impact
lenses.description: Who lost what? Put the loss next to the fine, the sentence and the recovery.
lenses.focus: Give every loss as a comparison: loss vs fine, fine vs profit, loss vs recovery, victims vs people compensated. Keep paper loss, cash loss and market value destroyed in separate lines.

lenses.name: What changed after
lenses.description: Which law, control or habit changed because of it, and did the change last?
lenses.focus: List the laws, rules and internal controls that changed because of this case, with dates. Then test whether each change held, using a later case or enforcement action.

lenses.name: Could it happen today
lenses.description: Run the scheme against today's controls. Which step still works?
lenses.focus: Take the mechanism and test it step by step against today's rules and tools. Say which step is closed, which is still open and which new tool opens a new route. Stay at red-flag level.

lenses.name: Penalty vs profit
lenses.description: Compare the money made with the money paid back. Who came out ahead?
lenses.focus: Do the crime math: gross proceeds or benefit, costs, fines, forfeiture, compensation, sentences. Compare with the firm's profit or revenue in the same period. State who came out ahead.

lenses.name: Who got away
lenses.description: Who was never charged or punished, and why?
lenses.focus: List who was involved but never charged, fined or sanctioned, with the documented reason (no evidence, immunity, cooperation, jurisdiction, time limit, death, flight). Do not speculate beyond sources.

lenses.name: The data trail
lenses.description: What pattern in the data would have flagged it, and what rule would catch it?
lenses.short: The rule that would have caught it
lenses.focus: Write the detection rule in plain English and as pseudo-SQL: the pattern, the threshold, the time window and the fields needed. List the likely false positives and what an analyst checks next.
